review: Recovery54 fixed-boundary same-input phase diagnostic candidate
assessment: The source fixture, production parser and test source stay unchanged. The new child verifies the exact parser file SHA256 and processing constant before building and checking the identical 195000385-byte one-million-row input and SHA256.

The observed function is a private copy of the exact whole-profile reader. Independently removing its four top-level constant phase callbacks yields the original function AST exactly; no control-flow, algorithm, validation or deadline statement changes.

The only boundaries are whole-document-validation, profile-schema, string-table and marker-columns. There are at most four callback invocations, no per-row hook, CPU profiler, sampling loop or new dependency.

The added observation runs as one owned child stage using the existing Runner, clean environment, actual job origin, phase15 and platform360 budgets and resource/unknown/cleanup limits. The exact six preflight stage names and typed exit/reap/group/cleanup fields are checked; the separate serializer stage remains independently checked.

The public phase value has exactly nine fields, one strict existing twelve-field density value and at most four two-field marks. Exact hashes, phase order, finite nondecreasing elapsed values, counter types and bounds, input identity and valid observed or processing-limit semantics are enforced in identical preflight and final validators.

The rows counter is second-pass marker entries, including the two controlled markers. Zero at an earlier boundary is a known counter value and does not mean the input has no rows or that document validation has completed.

A phase observation may validly be unconfirmed with null target counts and exit zero as a diagnostic procedure. It cannot promote the original failed QA suite: narrowly continued QA remains failed, its first-failure file is preserved and the final job remains failed.

If the original QA independently passes with an observed dense result, the current final gate can accept a valid unconfirmed extra phase observation. This preserves the diagnostic role of the extra stage; a later reader/long-readiness review must evaluate both observations rather than relabel the unconfirmed measurement as a pass.

Unexpected phase failure, invalid or private-extra receipt, cleanup failure, missing evidence or monitor failure cannot qualify the new observation. The original first failure is retained rather than replaced by later diagnostic failure.

independentValidation.guardInvocation: The successful independent guard execution explicitly supplies the QA module path; the initial invocation without that path stopped at the positive phase-validator import control. No production change was made for this invocation correction.
